data.gender_notes: Barrow is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Old English beorg or barrow, meaning 'hill' or 'barrow'. This name may have been given to someone living on a hill or to someone with a shining or bright personality. In the context of Christianity, it could be a reference to the hill where Jesus was crucified or the hill where He ascended into heaven. The name Barrow carries the meaning “Bright, shining hill” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Barrow usually hope their child will grow to embody bright, shining hill and live with faith, good character and purpose.

In 15th-century England, it was a common surname for people who lived near a hill or barrow, an ancient mound of earth or stones. In modern times, the name has spread globally and taken on new meanings and associations.

It can also represent the importance of lifting up one another in prayer and in deed, reaching new heights of faith together.
